verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser's own HyperAgent framework extends Playwright with AI so developers write natural-language commands instead of selectors, and page.ai() drives the page from described intents. The evidence shows a task-level page.ai() call, not discrete act/click/type primitives on described elements, and nothing documents resilience to selector or layout changes. Missing for 10: documented granular act/click/type primitives targeting described elements, evidence of robustness to selector/layout changes, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes

citations.quote: HyperAgent is an open-source browser automation framework that extends Playwright with AI capabilities. Write natural language commands instead of complex selectors
await page.ai("search for flights from Miami to LAX, select the cheapest option");
HyperAgent is our open-source tool that supercharges Playwright with AI.
